name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
summary: A hip-hinge that loads the hamstrings and glutes with a pair of dumbbells. It is easy to do at home and teaches the hinge pattern that carries over to deadlifts and jumping.
setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing you. Two filled backpacks or water-bottle jugs work as a home substitute.
Stand with feet hip-width apart and a soft bend in the knees.
Pull your shoulders back and down and brace your trunk.
execution: Push your hips straight back as if closing a door behind you with your glutes, keeping the knees only slightly bent.
Slide the dumbbells down close to your thighs and shins while your back stays flat.
Stop when you feel a strong stretch in the hamstrings, usually around mid-shin, before your back starts to round.
Squeeze your glutes and drive your hips forward to stand tall, keeping the weights close to your legs.
cues: Stand up by squeezing the glutes
mistakes: Rounding the lower back: shorten the range and only lower as far as you can keep a neutral spine.
Turning it into a squat by bending the knees a lot: keep the knees nearly fixed and move the hips back.
Letting the weights drift forward: keep them in contact with your thighs and shins.
Leaning back at the top: finish with hips under shoulders and ribs down instead of hyperextending.
